answer:
Based on the search results, the event after which they give out the MLB MVP award is the **World Series** (specifically, the season concluded by it). The team with the most World Series titles is the **New York Yankees** with 27 championships.

The New York Yankees' first World Series title was in **1923**.

Therefore, the opening day of the league (the 1923 season) would be **April 15, 1923**.

Answer: **April 15, 1923**

Title: Major League Baseball Most Valuable Player Award
Chunks: 3,4,5,6,25,26,27,28
Hank Greenberg, Stan Musial, Alex Rodriguez, Robin Yount, and Shohei Ohtani have won at different positions,[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Major_League_Baseball_Most_Valuable_Player_Award#cite_note-BD_2000-12) while Rodriguez is the only player who has won the award with two different teams at two different positions, and Ohtani the only one to do it at two positions in the same season (twice).[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Major_League_Baseball_Most_Valuable_Player_Award#cite_note-Rodriguez-14) Rodriguez and Andre Dawson are the only players to win the award while on a last-place team, the 2003 Texas Rangers and 1987 Chicago Cubs, respectively. Barry Bonds has won the most often (seven times) and the most consecutively (four from 2001 to 2004).[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Major_League_Baseball_Most_Valuable_Player_Award#cite_note-Bonds-15)Jimmie Foxx was the first player to win multiple times.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Major_League_Baseball_Most_Valuable_Player_Award#cite_note-Foxx-16) Ten players have won three times, and 19 have won twice.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Major_League_Baseball_Most_Valuable_Player_Award#cite_note-winner_list-17)Frank Robinson and Shohei Ohtani are the only players to win the award in both the American and National Leagues, with Ohtani being the first to win in both leagues in consecutive as well as multiple seasons.

The award's only tie occurred in the National League in 1979, when Keith Hernandez and Willie Stargell received an equal number of points.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Major_League_Baseball_Most_Valuable_Player_Award#cite_note-BD_2000-12)[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Major_League_Baseball_Most_Valuable_Player_Award#cite_note-1979_awards-18) There have been 23 unanimous winners, who received all the first-place votes.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Major_League_Baseball_Most_Valuable_Player_Award#cite_note-ESPN-3) The New York Yankees have the most winning players with 24, followed by the St. Louis Cardinals with 21 winners. The award has never been presented to a member of the following three teams: Arizona Diamondbacks, New York Mets, and Tampa Bay Rays.
In recent decades, pitchers have rarely won the award. When Ohtani won the AL award in 2021, he became the first pitcher in either league to be named the MVP since Clayton Kershaw in 2014, and the first in the American League since Justin Verlander in 2011. Ohtani also became the first two-way player to win the award [[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Major_League_Baseball_Most_Valuable_Player_Award#cite_note-19) and in 2023, he became the first player in MLB history to win MVP by unanimous vote twice.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Major_League_Baseball_Most_Valuable_Player_Award#cite_note-20) Since the creation of the Cy Young Award in 1956, he is the only pitcher to win an MVP award without winning a Cy Young in the same year (Don Newcombe, Sandy Koufax, Bob Gibson, Denny McLain, Vida Blue, Rollie Fingers, Willie Hernández, Roger Clemens, Dennis Eckersley, Verlander, and Kershaw all won a Cy Young award in their MVP seasons). In 2024, Ohtani became the first MVP winner to have played exclusively as a designated hitter in a season, a position that normally does not contribute on defense.

There was no award given by either league in 1930, which meant that one of the single greatest performances ever went unheralded when Hack Wilson of the Chicago Cubs set the current MLB record for RBI with 191.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Major_League_Baseball_Most_Valuable_Player_Award#cite_note-21) He also batted .356 and set the NL record with 56 HRs, a record which stood for 68 years until Mark McGwire (70) and Sammy Sosa (66) both eclipsed him.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Major_League_Baseball_Most_Valuable_Player_Award#cite_note-22)[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Major_League_Baseball_Most_Valuable_Player_Award#cite_note-23)

## Chalmers Award (1911–1914)
[edit]
Ty Cobb won the first American League Chalmers Award in 1911 and was at the center of the controversy over the previous season's award.
Before the 1910 season, Hugh Chalmers of Chalmers Automobile announced he would present a Chalmers Model 30 automobile to the player with the highest batting average in Major League Baseball at the end of the season. The 1910 race for best average in the American League was between the Detroit Tigers' widely disliked[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Major_League_Baseball_Most_Valuable_Player_Award#cite_note-ESPN-3)[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Major_League_Baseball_Most_Valuable_Player_Award#cite_note-26)[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Major_League_Baseball_Most_Valuable_Player_Award#cite_note-27)Ty Cobb and Nap Lajoie of the Cleveland Indians. On the last day of the season, Lajoie overtook Cobb's batting average with seven bunt hits against the St. Louis Browns.[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Major_League_Baseball_Most_Valuable_Player_Award#cite_note-LoC-28) American League President Ban Johnson said a recalculation showed that Cobb had won the race anyway, and Chalmers ended up awarding cars to both players.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Major_League_Baseball_Most_Valuable_Player_Award#cite_note-ESPN-3)
In the following season, Chalmers created the Chalmers Award. A committee of baseball writers was to convene after the season to determine the "most important and useful player to the club and the league." Since the award was not as effective at advertising as Chalmers had hoped, it was discontinued after 1914.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Major_League_Baseball_Most_Valuable_Player_Award#cite_note-ESPN-3)

Barry Bonds has won the most often (seven times) and the most consecutively (four from 2001 to 2004).[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Major_League_Baseball_Most_Valuable_Player_Award#cite_note-Bonds-15)Jimmie Foxx was the first player to win multiple times.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Major_League_Baseball_Most_Valuable_Player_Award#cite_note-Foxx-16) Ten players have won three times, and 19 have won twice.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Major_League_Baseball_Most_Valuable_Player_Award#cite_note-winner_list-17)Frank Robinson and Shohei Ohtani are the only players to win the award in both the American and National Leagues, with Ohtani being the first to win in both leagues in consecutive as well as multiple seasons.

The award's only tie occurred in the National League in 1979, when Keith Hernandez and Willie Stargell received an equal number of points.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Major_League_Baseball_Most_Valuable_Player_Award#cite_note-BD_2000-12)[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Major_League_Baseball_Most_Valuable_Player_Award#cite_note-1979_awards-18) There have been 23 unanimous winners, who received all the first-place votes.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Major_League_Baseball_Most_Valuable_Player_Award#cite_note-ESPN-3) The New York Yankees have the most winning players with 24, followed by the St. Louis Cardinals with 21 winners. The award has never been presented to a member of the following three teams: Arizona Diamondbacks, New York Mets, and Tampa Bay Rays.
In recent decades, pitchers have rarely won the award. When Ohtani won the AL award in 2021, he became the first pitcher in either league to be named the MVP since Clayton Kershaw in 2014, and the first in the American League since Justin Verlander in 2011. Ohtani also became the first two-way player to win the award [[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Major_League_Baseball_Most_Valuable_Player_Award#cite_note-19) and in 2023, he became the first player in MLB history to win MVP by unanimous vote twice.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Major_League_Baseball_Most_Valuable_Player_Award#cite_note-20) Since the creation of the Cy Young Award in 1956, he is the only pitcher to win an MVP award without winning a Cy Young in the same year (Don Newcombe, Sandy Koufax, Bob Gibson, Denny McLain, Vida Blue, Rollie Fingers, Willie Hernández, Roger Clemens, Dennis Eckersley, Verlander, and Kershaw all won a Cy Young award in their MVP seasons). In 2024, Ohtani became the first MVP winner to have played exclusively as a designated hitter in a season, a position that normally does not contribute on defense.

There was no award given by either league in 1930, which meant that one of the single greatest performances ever went unheralded when Hack Wilson of the Chicago Cubs set the current MLB record for RBI with 191.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Major_League_Baseball_Most_Valuable_Player_Award#cite_note-21) He also batted .356 and set the NL record with 56 HRs, a record which stood for 68 years until Mark McGwire (70) and Sammy Sosa (66) both eclipsed him.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Major_League_Baseball_Most_Valuable_Player_Award#cite_note-22)[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Major_League_Baseball_Most_Valuable_Player_Award#cite_note-23)

## Chalmers Award (1911–1914)
[edit]
Ty Cobb won the first American League Chalmers Award in 1911 and was at the center of the controversy over the previous season's award.
Before the 1910 season, Hugh Chalmers of Chalmers Automobile announced he would present a Chalmers Model 30 automobile to the player with the highest batting average in Major League Baseball at the end of the season. The 1910 race for best average in the American League was between the Detroit Tigers' widely disliked[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Major_League_Baseball_Most_Valuable_Player_Award#cite_note-ESPN-3)[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Major_League_Baseball_Most_Valuable_Player_Award#cite_note-26)[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Major_League_Baseball_Most_Valuable_Player_Award#cite_note-27)Ty Cobb and Nap Lajoie of the Cleveland Indians. On the last day of the season, Lajoie overtook Cobb's batting average with seven bunt hits against the St. Louis Browns.[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Major_League_Baseball_Most_Valuable_Player_Award#cite_note-LoC-28) American League President Ban Johnson said a recalculation showed that Cobb had won the race anyway, and Chalmers ended up awarding cars to both players.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Major_League_Baseball_Most_Valuable_Player_Award#cite_note-ESPN-3)
In the following season, Chalmers created the Chalmers Award. A committee of baseball writers was to convene after the season to determine the "most important and useful player to the club and the league." Since the award was not as effective at advertising as Chalmers had hoped, it was discontinued after 1914.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Major_League_Baseball_Most_Valuable_Player_Award#cite_note-ESPN-3)
